newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire army arrests deserters after river odyssey.
newsitem.headline: Zaire army arrests deserters after river odyssey.

text.p: Hundreds of Zairean soldiers who deserted after rebels drove them out of the eastern town of Goma have been arrested near the capital Kinshasa after an odyssey on hijacked barges down the River Zaire.

A Zairean military officer told Reuters that most of the deserters, who numbered more than 600, had been held since Friday in the riverside shanty town of Maluku, which merges with the sprawling capital's outer suburbs.
They would appear before a military tribunal, he said.
"Most of the soldiers handed themselves over, pleading that they had deserted because they had no more food or ammunition to carry on fighting," the officer said on Tuesday.

The deserters made their way from Goma to Kisangani, hundreds of kilometres (miles) away. "They hijacked two barges at Kisangani before floating downriver. They were stopped by the SARM (military intelligence) around 30 km (20 miles) upstream from Kinshasa," the officer said.
He said about 500 were crammed on one barge, about 150 on the other. Some fled and avoided capture.
Tutsi rebels who launched a revolt last month control most major towns bordering Tutsi-led Rwanda and Burundi. Zaire accuses Rwanda of invading, a charge it denies.
The fighting has put to flight hundreds of thousands of Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees and displaced several hundred thousand Zairean civilians.
The Rwandan Hutus fled in 1994, fearing reprisals after Hutu hardliners massacred up to a million minority Tutsis.
